WebAuthn vs OAuth 2.0: Which Architecture Actually Scales in Production? ⚡

• Throughput: OAuth 2.0 generally handles higher user volumes via token-based flows. WebAuthn's per-request cryptographic operations can introduce latency at extreme scales.
• Latency: WebAuthn's authentication process is typically faster for the end-user once registered. OAuth 2.0 involves redirects and token exchanges, adding overhead.
• Consistency: OAuth 2.0 offers more flexibility in managing session state and authorization across services. WebAuthn focuses purely on authentication, requiring integration with other systems for authorization.
• Failure Modes: OAuth 2.0 failures often relate to token expiration or invalid scopes. WebAuthn failures can stem from credential loss or device issues, requiring robust recovery mechanisms.
• Operational Overhead: OAuth 2.0 requires managing identity providers and token validation. WebAuthn requires secure credential management and user enrollment processes.

Recommendation: For pure authentication, WebAuthn offers superior security. For scalable authorization and federated identity, OAuth 2.0 is the industry standard. Many modern systems combine both.
